Cost assumptions

Labor estimate = operator count × hourly loaded rate × scheduled shift hours. Payback assumes the additional units can be sold and contribution is after variable costs.

User Manual
Process Simulator · v2.7.36 · Graphite interface

Quick start

Build a workflow, define the work at each station, assign people, then run and compare results.

  1. Choose File → New Blank Layout, or Load Example Scenario to explore the controls.
  2. Optionally import a floor-plan PDF and calibrate its scale.
  3. Add stations and connect them in process order. End each workflow at a Sink.
  4. Open Simulation → Process Sheet. Enter times in minutes, validate, and save.
  5. Open Simulation → Headcount Setup. Assign the people needed by the stations.
  6. Set days, shifts, target quantity, breaks, and efficiency in the Simulation menu. Click Run or Fast Run.
  7. Save the scenario and export the results you need.

The status strip at the bottom explains why a run cannot start. Resolve the stated process, routing, or headcount issue and run again.

Workspace and controls

The header shows the scenario filename. The command bar contains Station, Equipment, Undo, Run, Pause, Reset, and Speed. The metric strip shows current WIP, peak WIP, completed units, output per shift, and the limiting station.

Use View → Fit Layout to bring the layout into view. Zoom tools and the ruler are above the canvas. Select a station to edit it in the inspector; Edit station… opens the full form.

Graphite uses dark inset boxes for editable fields. Calculated values and fixed references appear on a lighter gray surface. Disabled fields remain readable and use a dashed border. Values in read-only cells are updated by the model, not typed into directly.

Use the playback controls below the layout to inspect recorded simulation history. Live / End returns to the current result.

Layout, PDF, and equipment

  1. In File, choose the PDF page number and select Import PDF Layout.
  2. Enter a known distance in Layout / Flow → Column spacing (ft). The default reference is 25 ft.
  3. Choose Calibrate Scale, then click two points separated by that distance.
  4. Use the PDF appearance selector above the layout to choose themed, high-contrast, or original appearance.

The themed PDF modes recolor the displayed drawing. Original appearance retains the imported image. Reports use the original background through the report renderer.

Add machines, benches, and other objects through Equipment Library. Use the selected equipment controls to set dimensions, rotation, station attachment, and lock state. Moving or resizing a graphic does not by itself define that station’s cycle time.

Use View → Display Sizes & Ruler for station symbols, labels, headcount symbols, and ruler visibility. Applying defaults affects new objects; the apply-to-all command changes existing station display sizes.

Stations and routes

Click Station, complete the form, choose Save & Place, and click the layout. Process performs work; Buffer holds a queue; Dwell / Cure represents dwell time; Sink records finished units.

Parallel positions controls simultaneous processing capacity. Buffer capacity sets waiting space, and Initial WIP sets starting inventory. The inspector’s staffing demand is a planning quantity; the headcount roster supplies actual people.

Choose Layout / Flow → Connect Stations, then select the source and destination. Use Disconnect Stations or the Route Editor to remove a route. Branching is supported; the run checks reject cycles and invalid origin/merge arrangements.

Select / Move returns to normal editing. Right-click an object for its available actions. Undo reverses supported model edits. Save before substantial changes.

Process Sheet

Open Simulation → Process Sheet. Each row is a station. Scroll horizontally for the full set of fields.

Field groupHow to use it
Operation / TypeEdit the station name and role.
Predecessor(s) / Successor(s)Read-only route references. Change connections in Layout / Flow.
Setup, Load, Manual, Machine / Dwell, Walk, Unload, InspectionEnter nonnegative times in minutes.
Calculated CTRead-only total, recalculated from the time components.
Parallel / Queue / Initial WIPProcessing positions, waiting capacity, and starting inventory.
Demand FTE / Labor Type / Shared GroupStation staffing information. Assign named people separately in Headcount Setup.
StatusRead the missing or invalid items and correct them before saving.

Calculated CT = setup time ÷ batch size + load + manual + machine/dwell + walk + unload + inspection. Buffer and Sink have zero process time.

Validate All checks the current entries. Save Process Sheet commits them to the model. Cancel closes without committing the sheet. Editing total CT in the inspector proportionally scales an existing time breakdown.

Some fields are stored for planning/export rather than used as a full simulation mechanism. Follow the field tooltips; do not assume that entering uptime, FPY, transfer quantity, or rework information creates stochastic failures or a rework model.

Headcount Setup

  1. Open Simulation → Headcount Setup and enter a person’s name.
  2. Select a station and enter that person’s FTE allocation.
  3. Use Add Station Assignment for additional responsibilities.
  4. Keep total allocation at or below 1.00 FTE per person, then click Add Person or the save action when editing.

For example, four allocations of 0.25 describe one person’s shift. The allocation status and roster table are read-only summaries; edit the assignment inputs to change them.

During a hands-on phase, an operator can serve only one station at a time. Machine/dwell time releases the operator for other work. Fractional station demand still rounds up to a whole-person requirement during a hands-on task; a 0.25 FTE demand does not create a quarter of a simultaneous operator.

Build Shared Roster from FTE offers a generated starting roster. Review its assignments before relying on the results. Show dots and Show station coverage control the layout overlays.

The walking-path controls select a person, origin, and destination. Where enabled, load a connection to edit waypoints. A drawn travel path is a visual route; enter the work’s Walk time in the Process Sheet rather than assuming path length automatically sets it.

Run and interpret results

The Simulation menu sets days, shifts per day, target units per workflow per shift, shift length, breaks, efficiency, and design WIP. Time inputs use minutes. The animation-speed selector changes playback speed.

Run animates the model. Pause stops advancement. Reset clears the run’s progress. Fast Run calculates the result without waiting for the animation.

Effective productive time per shift is (shift minutes − break minutes) × efficiency. Target quantity and productive time determine the planning takt and capacity comparisons. The Cure / dwell continues off-shift option controls off-shift dwell progression.

Current WIP is inventory in the workflow; peak WIP is the largest observed during the run; completed units are units reaching a sink. Constraint load compares station capacity against demand. A capacity warning is a model result that warrants checking the station’s time, parallel positions, and staffing.

Compare scenarios under the same settings. Save a baseline, change one assumption, rerun from reset, and compare throughput, WIP, and constraints.

Save, load, and reports

File → Save Scenario saves the model as JSON. Load Scenario / Excel accepts saved simulator JSON and Excel workbooks created by this simulator’s Export Excel function. It is not a generic spreadsheet importer.

Reports → Export Excel produces the workbook. Reports → Combined Report opens the consolidated report and its print controls. Reports use a light paper surface for readable printing.

The scenario filename appears in the interface and reports. Give alternatives distinct names, such as Baseline.json and Two_Operators.json. Save your work before closing the browser, starting a new layout, or loading the example.

Older scenarios can load using a compatibility model for cycle time and labor. Review the Process Sheet and Headcount Setup before treating an older scenario as a newly defined shared-labor model.

Troubleshooting

What you seeWhat to check
Run does not startRead the bottom status strip. Check Process Sheet completeness, routes, and assigned people.
A value cannot be editedCalculated CT and route references are read-only. Edit time components or routing instead. Disabled controls need the relevant object selected.
A station waits despite capacityCheck shared operators, upstream supply, queues, and downstream blocking.
A station is missing from viewUse Fit Layout and check zoom; show the inspector through View.
PDF looks too dark or too brightChange the PDF appearance mode. Check scale separately.
Process Sheet columns extend off-screenScroll the table horizontally. Its field text remains at a readable size.
Imported workbook is rejectedUse a workbook produced by this simulator, or load a simulator JSON file.
